chunks.text: 21-year-old male, Professional, resident of Clementi, Singapore.
Left wrist fracture in 2018 (healed, no hardware)
Allergic contact dermatitis to nickel (diagnosed age 12, resolved)
Elective knee arthroscopy for lateral meniscus tear repair (elective).
General Anesthesia with endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr. Tan. I'm Dr. Lim, the anesthesiologist who'll be taking care of you during your knee surgery today. Let me go through some questions to make sure everything's in order for your anesthesia plan.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Morning, Doctor. I'm ready when you are.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. First, can you tell me a bit about your knee problem? How long have you been having issues, and what led to the decision for surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Sure. I tore my meniscus playing football last year. Tried physio, but the pain kept coming back, especially when I twist or squat. Ortho said repair is the way to go lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Any other medical conditions like diabetes, high blood pressure, or heart issues?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Nope, all clear there. Just the knee.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. What medications are you currently taking, and have you stopped any recently?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I was on amoxicillin 500mg twice daily for a chest infection last month, but stopped it two weeks ago. That's all.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thanks. Now, about allergies—have you ever had a severe reaction to any antibiotics, including penicillin or related drugs?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh, yes! When I was 16, I had a really bad reaction to penicillin. Got a rash all over, then my throat swelled, and I couldn't breathe properly. Had to go to hospital lah. Never took penicillin again after that.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That sounds like anaphylaxis. Did you have hives, difficulty breathing, or low blood pressure at the time?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: All of that, Doctor. Rash came first, then I felt dizzy and couldn't catch my breath. Scared me half to death.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for sharing that. I'll update your records to reflect this penicillin allergy clearly. Have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, this is my first time under general anesthesia. Never even had a blood test before without fainting, haha.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Noted. How's your overall fitness? Can you walk up stairs or do daily activities without getting winded?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I can walk, but bending or twisting the knee hurts. Climbing stairs is slow, but I manage. No heart issues or shortness of breath otherwise.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Last question: when did you last eat or drink anything?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Had dinner at 8pm last night, water until midnight. Nothing since then, as instructed.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. We'll proceed with general anesthesia and intubation as planned. Your allergy will be flagged prominently, and we'll avoid all penicillin-related drugs. Any questions for me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, Doctor. Just want to get this sorted so I can play with my kids again without pain.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Absolutely. We'll take good care of you. I'll see you in the operating room shortly.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER

segments.speaker: PROVIDER

segments.speaker: PROVIDER

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] peripheral IV 20G placed

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:07] arterial line placed

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] 500 mL crystalloid bolus administered

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] mean arterial pressure dropped to 55 mmHg, treated with 1 mg phenylephrine

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:20] heart rate increased to 110 bpm, treated with 5 mL/kg fluid bolus

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I’m okay, but my knee is a bit painful.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: On a scale from 0 to 10, how would you rate the pain?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe around 4 or 5. It’s manageable, I think.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Any nausea or feeling like you want to vomit?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I’m not feeling sick at all.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: How’s your throat? Any discomfort from the tube during surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: A bit sore, but I can breathe fine. No problem.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Do you remember anything about the surgery itself?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Not really. I was out cold, I guess.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Any other issues you’re concerned about?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think that’s all. Thanks for checking on me.
